items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Shirley was as recently as 1990... We just happen to fortunately think quite alike when it comes to voicing but we disagreed quite a few times on chord choices... So she recorded as I recall what, three of your tunes

ctx.x: Would this be an appropriate time to just talk about who your favorite singers are, you’ve been mentioning a few.

Oh yeah, Peggy Lee for openers. Shirley Horn, I like singers that sound like they are singing in your ear. I don't like belters particularly that's a personal… but I can admire belters, I just don't like being yelled at, especially in love songs.
They’re not much fun to write for either.

items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I want to do the . . . for the writing team, the husband-and-wife writing team; they‘re brilliant. I want to do that songbook with Johnny Mandel.

ctx.x: Are there things . . . what do you foresee . . . well, what would you like to do still that you haven‘t done?

I want to go fishing so bad. Musically, right? I want to record with Oscar Peterson. I want to sit down and just sing with him. I want to do the same with Ahmad Jamal. I want to do the . . . for the writing team, the husband-and-wife writing team; they‘re brilliant. I want to do that songbook with Johnny Mandel. They wrote all that good music. What are their names? Good lord, CRS is really taking on. The Bergmans, you know the Bergmans songwriting team, husband and wife?
I probably know their songs, but I may not know their name.
